text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, hello. I'm Nasreen.
B: Gareth. Nice to meet you.
A: You too.
B: Whereabouts are you?
A: Walsall.
B: Not far. I'm Solihull.
A: Oh, Solihull is nice. Very nice houses.
B: Some of them. We're in a new-build in Shirley. Four-bed. It does us.
A: Four bedrooms. Very nice.
B: What do you do?
A: Erm, I'm between jobs at the moment. Before, I was receptionist at a GP surgery.
B: My mum did that. Reception at a GP's in Acocks Green. Twenty-odd years.
A: Really? Then she knows. It's very hard job, people don't think.
B: Yeah. She used to come home and say who'd shouted at her that day. Never seemed to bother her much, though.
A: You have to be patient. Some people, they are worried, they are not well, so they shout. You just, erm, you let them talk, and you say, I understand, I will try. Most of the time they calm down. And the old people, they just want somebody to listen, you know. I liked that part. The filing, not so much.
B: Ha. No, I can imagine.
A: What do you do?
B: Quantity surveyor. Commercial manager for a contractor. We build hospitals and schools.
A: Hospitals. So you are building, like, the new one?
B: Not the building myself. I do the money side. Costs, payments.
A: Acha. Very important job.
B: It keeps me busy. Fifty-odd hours most weeks.
A: That's a lot. Your family must miss you.
B: They're used to it. Two kids, eleven and eight.
A: Still small. Do they like school?
B: They do alright. I keep an eye on the grades. My lad's got his SATs this year, so that's the focus.
A: My son is doing A-levels. Seventeen. He wants university.
B: Good. What's he doing?
A: Maths, business, and, erm, computer something. ICT.
B: Sensible choices. Tell him to look at Aston or Birmingham City. I did BCU. First in my family to go.
A: He will also be first. On my side.
B: Good for him.
A: Yes. Inshallah.
B: Do you get into Birmingham much?
A: Sometimes, for my daughter. And Soho Road, for Eid, the sweets.
B: I'm more Stratford Road. There's a curry place we go Fridays.
A: Which one?
B: Er, I'd have to—
